patch.value: Linear-space divide-and-conquer diff, for an absolute memory ceiling the band bound cannot give

The banded trace from pm-vcs-ze24 bounds each snapshot to the 2d plus 1 reachable diagonals, which turns the trace from d times combined width into d squared. That is a real and provable win, but it is a relative one. The trace is still quadratic in the edit distance, so two ten-thousand-line files with nothing in common still hold roughly 1.6 gibibytes of live Int32 storage against the 3.2 gibibytes the full-width version paid. Raised by CodeRabbit on pull request 21, which correctly observed that comparing the banded total against the rectangular total is an inequality holding for every input and therefore bounds nothing in absolute terms.

The diff computes an edit script for two ten-thousand-line files with no common lines inside a fixed memory ceiling that does not grow with the edit distance, using the linear-space divide-and-conquer form of the algorithm in which the middle snake is located from a forward and a reverse pass and the two halves are recursed into. Edit scripts stay byte-identical to the current banded implementation across the existing randomized and edge-shaped equivalence corpus. The pathological ten-thousand-line case runs in the default suite rather than behind an opt-in environment variable, because it no longer depends on the runner having gibibytes free.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Raised by CodeRabbit on pull request 21 with the arithmetic spelled out: at size 10000 the edit distance is 20000, so the banded total is (20001) squared equals 400040001 Int32 entries, about 1.6 gibibytes, and every one of the 20001 snapshots stays reachable until the backtrack returns. The reviewer also noted the only budget assertion compared the banded total against the rectangular total, an inequality true for every input. Both points were correct. The test now asserts the budget in bytes against the closed form and the full ten-thousand-line size is opt-in behind PM_VCS_DIFF_PATHOLOGICAL_SIZE, so a routine run no longer depends on 1.6 gibibytes being free.
